ucs.title: [LLM] Earth Lusca (Aquatic Panda) web shell post-exploit reconnaissance from IIS/Exchange/Tomcat worker processes
ucs.description: Hunts the characteristic Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda / Charcoal Typhoon initial-access-to-recon chain: exploitation of an internet-facing application (ProxyLogon/ProxyShell, Log4Shell, Confluence, GlassFish) drops a China Chopper / Behinder / Godzilla / AntSword web shell, after which the web-server worker (w3wp.exe, java.exe, tomcat*.exe, httpd.exe) spawns native enumeration LOLBins. This parent->child pair almost never occurs in benign IIS/Tomcat workloads and is one of the highest-fidelity Earth Lusca signatures Trend Micro, CrowdStrike, and Microsoft have published on the cluster.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","tomcat*.exe","java.exe","cgi-fcgi.exe","php-cgi.exe")) (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","hostname.exe","quser.exe","nltest.exe","arp.exe","route.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","wmic.exe","vssadmin.exe")) by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | rename Processes.* as * | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM" OR process_name IN ("whoami.exe","nltest.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","quser.exe") | sort 0 - lastTime
ucs.kql:
// Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda — web-shell-spawned native recon LOLBin under IIS/Tomcat/Java worker
let WebWorkers = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","java.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","cgi-fcgi.exe","php-cgi.exe"]);
let ReconLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","hostname.exe","quser.exe","nltest.exe","arp.exe","route.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","wmic.exe","vssadmin.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (WebWorkers)
| where FileName in~ (ReconLolbins)
// Earth Lusca tooling characteristically chains discovery — score by chain depth
| summarize ReconBinariesSeen = dcount(FileName),
            DistinctChildren = make_set(FileName, 32),
            SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 8),
            ParentCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 4),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            EventCount = count()
            by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where ReconBinariesSeen >= 2 or (ReconBinariesSeen == 1 and EventCount >= 3)   // chained-recon > one-off; tune for IIS-heavy estates
| extend ChainHint = case(set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"whoami.exe") and set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"net.exe"), "China-Chopper-style",
                          set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"powershell.exe") and set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"certutil.exe"), "Behinder/Godzilla-style",
                          "generic-webshell-recon")
| order by LastSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Earth Lusca — IIS/Tomcat worker spawning native recon LOLBin (Sentinel SecurityEvent 4688 path)
let WebWorkers = dynamic(["w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","java.exe","tomcat.exe","tomcat9.exe","tomcat10.exe","cgi-fcgi.exe","php-cgi.exe"]);
let ReconLolbins = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","hostname.exe","quser.exe","nltest.exe","arp.exe","route.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","wmic.exe","vssadmin.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentLeaf = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildLeaf  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,  "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentLeaf in (WebWorkers)
| where ChildLeaf  in (ReconLolbins)
| summarize ReconBinariesSeen = dcount(ChildLeaf),
            DistinctChildren  = make_set(ChildLeaf, 32),
            SampleCmds        = make_set(CommandLine, 8),
            FirstSeen         = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen          = max(TimeGenerated),
            EventCount        = count()
            by Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentLeaf, ParentProcessName
| where ReconBinariesSeen >= 2 or (ReconBinariesSeen == 1 and EventCount >= 3)
| extend ChainHint = case(set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"whoami.exe") and set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"net.exe"), "China-Chopper-style",
                          set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"powershell.exe") and set_has_element(DistinctChildren,"certutil.exe"), "Behinder/Godzilla-style",
                          "generic-webshell-recon")
| order by LastSeen desc

ucs.title: [LLM] Earth Lusca LSASS credential dump via rundll32 + comsvcs.dll MiniDump
ucs.description: Catches Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda / Bronze University's signature LSASS dumping technique: invoking the built-in comsvcs.dll MiniDump export through rundll32 to extract credentials without touching procdump.exe. The actor has used this LOLBin-only variant repeatedly (documented by Trend Micro, Secureworks, and CrowdStrike on the Aquatic Panda VMware Horizon/Log4Shell intrusions) because comsvcs.dll is signed by Microsoft and present on every Windows host. This UC fires on the exact rundll32 invocation pattern and on suspicious comsvcs.dll image-loads into non-svchost processes.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd values(Processes.process_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" (Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs*#-24*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs*,#24*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll, MiniDump*") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | rename Processes.* as * | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort 0 - lastTime
ucs.kql:
// Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda — LSASS dump via comsvcs.dll MiniDump LOLBin
// Two paths: (1) rundll32 invocation pattern, (2) comsvcs.dll loaded into a non-LSASS-adjacent process touching lsass
let RundllInvocation = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "comsvcs"
          and (ProcessCommandLine has "MiniDump"
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)comsvcs(?:\.dll)?\s*[, ]\s*#?\s*24\b"   // ordinal #24 = MiniDump
               or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)#-?24\b")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
              ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
              Path = "rundll32-comsvcs-MiniDump";
let SuspiciousLoad = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "comsvcs.dll"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("svchost.exe","dllhost.exe","services.exe","explorer.exe","taskhostw.exe","sihost.exe","msiexec.exe")
    | join kind=inner (
        DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
        | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("lsass","MiniDump","sekurlsa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, RelatedCmd = ProcessCommandLine
    ) on DeviceName, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildCmd    = RelatedCmd,
              ChildSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              Path = "comsvcs-loaded-into-non-svchost+lsass-keyword";
RundllInvocation
| union SuspiciousLoad
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda — comsvcs.dll MiniDump via rundll32 (Sentinel 4688 path)
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ChildLeaf = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ChildLeaf == "rundll32.exe"
| where CommandLine has "comsvcs"
      and (CommandLine has "MiniDump"
           or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)comsvcs(?:\.dll)?\s*[, ]\s*#?\s*24\b"
           or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)#-?24\b")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType, LogonId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Earth Lusca LSASS Memory Dump via Rundll32 + comsvcs.dll MiniDump
id: 9b3b1d0e-2c0a-4f1d-9a0e-3b1a1f0c0002
status: experimental
description: Detects the LOLBin LSASS-dump primitive used by Earth Lusca / Aquatic Panda / Bronze University -- rundll32.exe invoking the MiniDump export (ordinal #24) of the Microsoft-signed comsvcs.dll to extract LSASS memory without dropping procdump or mimikatz on disk.
references:
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/22/d/Earth-Lusca-Uses-New-Techniques-and-Toolset.html
  - https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/falcon-overwatch-team-finds-novel-aquatic-panda-activity/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0143/
  - https://lolbas-project.github.io/lolbas/Libraries/Comsvcs/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/21
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1003.001
  - attack.t1218.011
  - attack.g0143
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_rundll32:
    Image|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_payload:
    - CommandLine|contains|all:
        - 'comsvcs'
        - 'MiniDump'
    - CommandLine|re: '(?i)comsvcs(\.dll)?\s*[, ]\s*#?\s*24\b'
  filter_machine_account:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection_rundll32 and selection_payload and not filter_machine_account
falsepositives:
  - Authorised red-team / IR collection of LSASS memory for forensic triage
level: critical
ucs.datadog_query: source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @Image:(*\rundll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\Rundll32.exe) (@CommandLine:(*comsvcs*MiniDump* OR *Comsvcs*MiniDump* OR *COMSVCS*MINIDUMP* OR *comsvcs.dll,#24* OR *comsvcs.dll, #24* OR *comsvcs,#24*)) -@SubjectUserName:*$
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\rundll32\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)comsvcs", field=CommandLine)
| (regex("(?i)minidump", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)comsvcs(\\.dll)?\\s*[, ]\\s*#?\\s*24\\b", field=CommandLine))
| NOT (UserName=/\$$/)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(as=Hits), collect([CommandLine, SHA256HashData], multival=true), min(@timestamp, as=FirstSeen), max(@timestamp, as=LastSeen)])
| sort(field=LastSeen, order=desc)
ucs.rationale: CrowdStrike OverWatch's Aquatic Panda intrusion writeup (VMware Horizon / Log4Shell, Dec 2021) and Trend Micro's Earth Lusca dossier explicitly document this exact LOLBin -- rundll32 + comsvcs.dll!MiniDump -- as the actor's preferred credential-dump primitive because it leaves no novel binary on disk. The ordinal-#24 invocation form (e.g. 'rundll32 comsvcs.dll #24 <pid> dump.bin full') is rare eno
